newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya's Gaddafi arrives in Tunisia.
newsitem.headline: Libya's Gaddafi arrives in Tunisia.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi on Monday crossed the Libyan-Tunisian land border on his way to Tunis for a visit at the invitation of President Zine al-Abidine Ben Ali, the official Libyan news agency JANA said.
JANA, in its first report on the visit, said Gaddafi crossed the border at dawn.

Gaddafi travelled by land because Libya has been under a United Nations flight embargo since 1992 for failing to hand over two suspects in the bombing of a U.S. airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland, for trial in the West.
Gaddafi was due to travel through several Tunisian cities on his way to the capital.
He was expected to reach Tunis in the afternoon and join Ben Ali on a tour of the city centre for a popular welcome.
Diplomatic sources said the visit would last about a week.
Ben Ali and Gaddafi last met in January for a few hours at the border.
Both countries are members of the Arab Maghreb Union, a regional economic and political grouping set up in 1989 with Algeria, Mauritania and Morocco.
